prompt: A team creates an uplink-free standard switch for two compatible same-host lab guests. Which expectation is reasonable?
options: Local communication can work, but this alone provides no external LAN path
All guest networking is impossible until an uplink exists
The switch automatically routes them to the Internet
Every local frame must go through a physical router
en: Local switching and external connectivity have different path requirements.
ru: Local switching aur external connectivity ki path requirements alag hain.

prompt: An administrator types a host management address into notes under vSwitch0. Which clarification is needed?
options: The address belongs to a VMkernel interface attached through the management group
The switch label itself owns every guest IP
The datastore owns the management IP
Every vmnic must be assigned that same static IP
en: The switch forwards frames; the VMkernel interface is the host IP endpoint.
ru: Switch frames forward karta hai; VMkernel interface host IP endpoint hai.

prompt: Two standalone hosts each have a vSwitch0. A change on one does not appear on the other. What explains this?
options: Standard switches are configured per host
Identical names guarantee a shared distributed configuration
DNS replication should copy their switch settings
The unchanged host must be powered off
en: Matching labels do not turn local standard switches into a shared distributed switch.
ru: Matching labels local standard switches ko shared distributed switch nahin banate.

prompt: A SERVERS group was created, but a guest is still attached to another network. What is required to use SERVERS?
options: Select the intended group for its virtual NIC and verify guest configuration/path
Only rename the guest disk SERVERS
Only create an A record matching the label
Assume creation moved every guest automatically
en: Creation of a network object does not attach guests automatically.
ru: Network object banana guests ko automatically attach nahin karta.

prompt: Only one group fails after a switch teaming change. Other groups work. What should be inspected?
options: That group’s effective policy and overrides
Only the shared DNS suffix
Only the VM disk capacity
Only the order of switch names
en: A group override may differ from the parent switch’s settings.
ru: Group override parent switch settings se mukhtalif ho sakta hai.

prompt: Blue and Green groups use the same switch and same untagged network. What isolation claim is unsupported?
options: Different names alone create separate security boundaries
Both groups may exist on the switch
Guest addressing still needs configuration
Policies and upstream design matter
en: Names do not independently segment the Layer-2 network.
ru: Names independently Layer-2 network segment nahin karte.

prompt: A candidate vmnic is already assigned elsewhere. Why must that assignment be considered before moving it?
options: A vmnic cannot belong to two standard switches simultaneously
The adapter must first become a DNS secondary
The switch needs a matching Windows user name
The adapter must use a port-group label as its IP
en: Assignment ownership must be reconciled before reassignment.
ru: Reassignment se pehle existing assignment ownership handle honi chahiye.

prompt: Nested ESXi reports 10 Gbit/s Full, but a transfer runs at 80 Mbit/s. What is a valid interpretation?
options: Reported virtual link speed is not an end-to-end throughput guarantee
The transfer rate is mathematically impossible
ESXi must have measured Internet speed incorrectly
The guest must be on VLAN 80
en: CPU, endpoints and outer networking can limit throughput below reported virtual link speed.
ru: CPU, endpoints aur outer networking throughput ko reported virtual link speed se kam kar sakte hain.

prompt: A Workstation test should disconnect one spare nested uplink. What evidence identifies the correct adapter?
options: Current MAC matching and its outer network/management role
Assuming adapter order always matches vmnic numbers
Choosing any adapter labelled Connected
Disabling the desktop’s physical Ethernet first
en: Map the intended test link and preserve management before simulating a fault.
ru: Fault simulate karne se pehle test link map aur management preserve karein.

prompt: An interface named vmk1 has a storage IP. Which claim still requires additional evidence?
options: An NFS or iSCSI datastore is connected and passing I/O
The captured interface has an IP value
A VMkernel object exists at that checkpoint
The storage label is displayed
en: Network creation is not protocol/session/datastore verification.
ru: Network creation protocol/session/datastore verification nahin.

prompt: Existing vmk1 is 172.16.0.102/16. A new isolated exercise proposes 172.16.50.0/24. Which plan is careful?
options: Detect overlap and choose a verified non-overlapping design before implementation
Assume different third octets always mean different connected networks
Apply both without checking routes
Change the management gateway to 172.16.50.1 by guess
en: The /24 lies inside the /16, so the example needs deliberate addressing review.
ru: /24, /16 ke andar hai; example ki addressing deliberate review mangti hai.

prompt: A storage test succeeds through the default host path, but the intended storage vmk is uncertain. What is useful?
options: Inspect actual interfaces/routes and test explicitly through the intended vmk
Always use vmk0 because it is first
Assume every interface passed the same test
Delete the unknown interface immediately
en: A successful unspecified path does not verify every VMkernel interface.
ru: Unspecified path ki success har VMkernel interface verify nahin karti.

prompt: Same-host VLAN 30 peers work, but a physical VLAN 30 peer fails. Which path needs investigation?
options: The tagged uplink, outer/upstream VLAN path and endpoint settings
Only the local guest disk format
Only the group’s display capitalization
Assume local success proves trunk compatibility
en: Local traffic can avoid the external tagged path entirely.
ru: Local traffic external tagged path ko bilkul avoid kar sakti hai.

prompt: Guests use different IP subnets on one untagged Layer-2 network. What cannot be concluded from addressing alone?
options: That a secure Layer-2 isolation boundary exists
That the chosen IP prefixes differ
That routing may be needed for ordinary inter-subnet traffic
That the network configuration needs inspection
en: Subnets describe addressing; Layer-2 separation needs topology/policy evidence.
ru: Subnets addressing batati hain; Layer-2 separation ko topology/policy evidence chahiye.

prompt: A name resolves correctly, but a VLAN mismatch blocks the destination path. What will another identical lookup fix by itself?
options: Nothing in the incompatible VLAN path
It automatically retags all frames
It creates the missing upstream trunk
It moves the VM to the destination port group
en: DNS returns an address; it does not repair Layer-2 path configuration.
ru: DNS address deta hai; Layer-2 path configuration repair nahin karta.

prompt: A link fault test shows a local same-host ping uninterrupted. What is still needed to assess uplink recovery?
options: Traffic to an external endpoint that crosses the tested uplinks
Only longer local pings on the same switch
Only a screenshot of two Active entries
Only a DNS record for the backup NIC
en: The test path must exercise the mechanism being claimed.
ru: Test path ko claimed mechanism actually exercise karna chahiye.

prompt: Both nested links are Active but share one Windows host and physical NIC. What survives as a common risk?
options: Failure of the shared physical host/NIC can affect both
No risk remains because the virtual names differ
The second virtual NIC automatically uses another building
Active/Active guarantees independent power supplies
en: Multiple virtual paths do not guarantee independent physical infrastructure.
ru: Multiple virtual paths independent physical infrastructure guarantee nahin karte.

prompt: An upstream router fails while local NIC links remain Up under Link status only. What explains absent failover?
options: The monitored local link state may not reflect that upstream fault
The policy continuously tests every remote application
The DNS primary suffix controls link detection
Unused adapters always become Active on every timeout
en: Detection scope matters; not every upstream fault becomes link-down.
ru: Detection scope matter karta hai; har upstream fault link-down nahin banta.

prompt: A baseline is 6 Mbit/s and the proposed sustained cap is 10 Mbit/s. Why may the cap have no visible effect?
options: An existing lower bottleneck limits the test before the cap
Shaping guarantees throughput will rise to the cap
Peak always multiplies baseline performance
A cap can only be tested with DNS packets
en: A limit higher than achievable throughput need not become the bottleneck.
ru: Achievable throughput se upar limit lazmi bottleneck nahin banti.

prompt: A plan lists average/peak in Kbit/s and burst in KB. Which distinction matters?
options: Average/peak are rates; burst is a quantity of data
All values are rates with interchangeable units
Burst is the maximum number of VMkernel adapters
Average applies to ping only and peak to HTTP only
en: Rate, data amount and application type are different concepts.
ru: Rate, data amount aur application type alag concepts hain.

prompt: An outbound VM-A cap affects sending to a peer. A reverse bulk-data test differs. What must the review consider?
options: Traffic direction, acknowledgments, effective policy and other bottlenecks
Assume the same bulk-data cap is guaranteed both ways
Assume reverse testing disables all shaping
Assume any difference proves missing DNS records
en: The standard-switch endpoint outbound policy is directional.
ru: Standard-switch endpoint outbound policy directional hai.

prompt: TCP 443 succeeds, but Host Client does not load. What is the focused next investigation?
options: HTTPS/TLS, browser/proxy and management application behavior
Assume login is already verified
Delete vmk0 immediately
Reset all storage adapters first
en: Transport connection success does not establish successful page loading or authentication.
ru: Transport connection success page loading ya authentication establish nahin karti.

prompt: Normal Windows name resolution works through hosts, but nslookup finds no DNS record. What is the likely conceptual distinction?
options: Local hosts mappings and DNS server queries are separate paths
Every SSH alias is automatically a public A record
nslookup proves all networking is broken
A hosts entry must create a secondary zone
en: A working local mapping does not prove server-side DNS data.
ru: Working local mapping server-side DNS data ka proof nahin.

prompt: A historical screenshot differs from the running inventory. How should a repeat lab proceed?
options: Record the current state and reconcile checkpoints before scoped changes
Force every setting back to the oldest screenshot
Assume current assignments are invalid because they changed
Invent missing intermediate outputs
en: Historical evidence is useful context, not a substitute for present-state checks.
ru: Historical evidence useful context hai, present-state checks ka badal nahin.

prompt: A browser failure disappears without a captured cause test. What belongs in the incident conclusion?
options: Later access succeeded; the original exact cause remains unconfirmed
DNS definitely caused it because the symptom involved a name
A cable fault is certain even though links were not checked
All future management access is guaranteed
en: Symptom recovery and proof of root cause are distinct findings.
ru: Symptom recovery aur root cause ka proof alag findings hain.
